meta.abstract: Dell Technologies Inc. (DELL, NYSE) is the integrated technology hardware and infrastructure platform built around the 1984 founding company of the same name, now Chairman and CEO Michael Dell's franchise at $113.5 billion of FY2026 revenue (fiscal year ended approximately January 30 2026) and approximately $43 billion of AI server backlog entering FY2027. The company operates two reportable segments: Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) — servers, storage, networking, AI Factory — which generated $18.82 billion in Q4 FY26 (+66% YoY) on the back of $24.6 billion of full-year AI server revenue (+300%+ YoY) and over $64 billion of AI-optimised server orders closed during FY26 with $25+ billion of AI server shipments; and Client Solutions Group (CSG) — commercial and consumer PCs — which generated $13.5 billion in Q4 (+14% YoY) with commercial $11.6 billion (+16%) and consumer $1.9 billion (flat). The executive bench combines Michael Dell as Chairman and CEO with Jeff Clarke as Vice Chairman and COO (running CSG, ISG, and Global Supply Chain since December 2019), Chuck Whitten as the post-Bain joined-2021 commercial co-leader, Bill Scannell as global sales leader (30+ years at Dell), and David Kennedy as interim CFO from September 2025 following Yvonne McGill's announced transition (after nearly 30 years at Dell including CFO since 2023; remains in advisory capacity through Q3 fiscal 2026). The board is anchored by Michael Dell as Chairman alongside Ellen Kullman (Lead Independent Director, ex-DuPont CEO, Carbon Inc. Executive Chair), Egon Durban (Silver Lake Co-CEO, board since October 2013), David Dorman (Founding Partner Centerview Capital Technology), William Green (ex-Accenture Chairman, Audit Committee Chair), David Grain (Grain Management founder/CEO), Steven Mollenkopf (ex-Qualcomm CEO), and Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich. The board has unanimously recommended Dell's redomestication to Texas. The investment proposition compresses the AI server demand cycle, customer-supply alignment with Nvidia + AMD + hyperscaler buyers, AI PC refresh cycle in CSG, and the operating-leverage opportunity as the ISG mix shifts toward AI server revenue — against execution risk on the $43B backlog ramp, AI capex cyclicality, and competition from HPE / Supermicro / Lenovo / direct hyperscaler ODMs.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## The Numbers That Reset The Frame

Dell entered fiscal 2027 with disclosures that materially changed how the market read the company. It reported $113.5 billion of FY2026 revenue, $24.683 billion of AI-optimised-server revenue, more than $64 billion of AI-optimised-server orders closed during the year, more than $25 billion of AI-optimised-server shipments, and a $43 billion backlog entering the new fiscal year. On Dell's own numbers, AI-optimised servers accounted for roughly one-fifth of annual revenue. A year earlier, Dell had said it shipped $9.8 billion of AI-optimised servers in FY2025 and had booked deals with xAI and others that left backlog at roughly $9 billion. The scale change between those two year-end disclosures defined the new investment debate around the company. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3) [Dell Q4 FY2025 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

Dell's Class C common stock traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker **DELL**, and its principal executive offices remained at One Dell Way in Round Rock, Texas. Michael S. Dell continued to serve as chairman and chief executive officer of the company he founded in 1984. Jeff Clarke, whom Dell elevated to vice chairman and chief operating officer in December 2019, oversaw the two operating segments and global operations. The finance transition was also settled before the end of the window: Dell had appointed David Kennedy chief financial officer on an interim basis effective 9 September 2025, kept Yvonne McGill in an advisory role through the third quarter of fiscal 2026, and then named Kennedy chief financial officer on a permanent basis on 25 November 2025. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Appoints Jeff Clarke Vice Chairman and COO](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/2019/12/20191202-01.htm) [Dell CFO Transition Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2025~09~dell-technologies-announces-cfo-transition.htm) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial)

## Two Segments, One Clear Shift

Dell still reported through two operating segments. Infrastructure Solutions Group, or ISG, produced $60.826 billion of FY2026 revenue and $7.111 billion of operating income. Client Solutions Group, or CSG, produced $50.984 billion of revenue and $2.833 billion of operating income. By the fourth quarter the mix shift was unmistakable: ISG delivered record quarterly revenue of $19.6 billion, including record quarterly AI-optimised-server revenue of $9.0 billion, while CSG delivered $13.5 billion, with commercial client revenue of $11.6 billion and consumer revenue of $1.9 billion. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

| Segment / line | FY2026 revenue | Q4 FY2026 revenue | Operating income / margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ISG | $60.826B | $19.6B | $7.111B / 11.7% |
| CSG | $50.984B | $13.5B | $2.833B / 5.6% |
| AI-optimised servers | $24.683B | $9.0B | not separately disclosed |
| Commercial client | $44.062B | $11.6B | included in CSG |
| Consumer | $6.922B | $1.9B | included in CSG |

## Governance For The Next Cycle

Dell's 2026 proxy named eight directors for election: Michael Dell, Ellen Kullman, Egon Durban, David Dorman, David Grain, William Green, Steven Mollenkopf and Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich. The board also backed a move to change Dell's state of incorporation from Delaware to Texas and said stockholders would vote on that proposal at the annual meeting scheduled for 25 June 2026. That mattered less as an operating catalyst than as a signal that the board was aligning legal domicile with the company's long-standing Texas operating centre. [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm) [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication)

## The Central Analytical Question

Dell's own filings made the analytical problem narrower and more demanding. The question was not whether demand existed; more than $64 billion of orders and a $43 billion backlog answered that. The question was whether Dell could convert that backlog into revenue without giving up too much margin in the process. The 10-K said ISG operating margin fell to 11.7 per cent from 12.8 per cent because gross margin rate declined primarily on a richer mix of AI-optimised servers. The bull case therefore rested on scale and backlog conversion; the bear case rested on timing, customer concentration and mix-driven profitability pressure. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Backlog Ladder

The year-end backlog did not appear from nowhere. Dell had already disclosed $14.4 billion of AI backlog at the end of the first quarter, then said first-half AI shipments had reached $10 billion by the second quarter, then reported $18.4 billion of backlog at the end of the third quarter before closing FY2026 at $43 billion. Read in sequence, those figures showed both the scale of demand and the extent to which fulfilment lagged booking even after a major shipping ramp. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Board Around Michael Dell

Dell's proxy also made clear that the board around Michael Dell was small and continuity-oriented. Ellen Kullman remained lead independent director. Egon Durban remained the long-running Silver Lake representative from the take-private era. William Green chaired the audit committee, while Steven Mollenkopf gave the board a former semiconductor chief executive with direct exposure to the chip industry that now sat at the centre of Dell's infrastructure cycle. That composition reinforced the point that Dell was approaching the AI build-out with the same governance bench that had already overseen the EMC acquisition, the VMware spin-off and the balance-sheet simplification that came before this cycle. [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

chapters.title: From the UT-Austin dorm room to the AI server giant
chapters.body:
## The Dorm Room And The Direct Model

Dell's own corporate timeline remained the cleanest primary source for the company's early history. Michael Dell started PCs Limited in 1984 with $1,000, incorporated the company in May of that year, renamed it Dell Computer Corporation in 1987, and took it public in June 1988 in a $30 million initial public offering. The operating idea was simple and durable: sell directly to the customer, assemble to order, and reduce the inventory risk that came with the traditional reseller channel. By 2001, Dell said it had become the world's No. 1 computer systems company. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline)

That operating model mattered because it explained why Dell later found it easier than many rivals to pivot from consumer and corporate PCs into more complex enterprise systems. The company was built around configuration, procurement discipline and direct customer relationships rather than around a retail shelf. Those same habits - buying components at scale, building to demand, and keeping the sales relationship close to the end user - later translated into servers, storage and, eventually, AI infrastructure. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline)

## The Take-Private And The Enterprise Pivot

Dell's modern structure was the product of three large capital-markets events rather than one continuous line from the 1990s PC franchise. First came the 2013 take-private. Dell's timeline described Michael Dell and Silver Lake as taking the company private in the largest leveraged buyout in technology history, a transaction valued at $24.9 billion. Egon Durban joined the board in that period and remained there through every major step that followed. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

Second came EMC. Dell announced the EMC transaction in 2015 and completed it on 7 September 2016, creating Dell Technologies and bringing VMware, the EMC storage franchise and a much larger enterprise-customer footprint under one roof. The deal was widely described as the largest technology acquisition completed to that point, and it changed the company's economic mix permanently: the Dell story ceased to be mainly about PCs and became a story about client devices plus enterprise infrastructure. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline)

Third came the unwind of the VMware structure. Dell returned to public trading on the NYSE in December 2018 through an exchange tied to the VMware tracking stock rather than through a conventional IPO. It then completed the VMware spin-off in 2021. The sequence simplified the structure, returned direct public-market visibility to Dell, and started the deleveraging phase that left the company better prepared for the capital intensity of the AI-server cycle. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

## The AI Inflection

FY2025 and FY2026 marked a clear break from the pre-AI period, and the official sequence was more precise than the market shorthand around it. Dell's FY2025 year-end release on 27 February 2025 said it shipped $9.8 billion of AI-optimised servers during the year and had booked deals with xAI and others that left backlog at roughly $9 billion. That was the first point at which Dell used a named customer in a primary year-end AI disclosure. [Dell Q4 FY2025 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2)

The FY2026 cadence then showed the ramp quarter by quarter. On 29 May 2025, Dell said first-quarter revenue was $23.4 billion and that it had generated $12.1 billion of AI orders in the quarter, exiting with $14.4 billion of AI backlog. On 28 August 2025, it said second-quarter revenue had risen to $29.8 billion, that first-half AI-server shipments had reached $10 billion, and that full-year AI-server shipment guidance had been raised to more than $20 billion. On 25 November 2025, it reported third-quarter revenue of $27.0 billion, another $12.3 billion of AI orders, nearly $30 billion of AI orders year to date, an $18.4 billion AI backlog, and a full-year AI-server shipment outlook of roughly $25 billion. On 26 February 2026, it closed the loop with $24.683 billion of full-year AI-optimised-server revenue, more than $64 billion of orders closed in FY2026, more than $25 billion of shipments, and a $43 billion backlog entering FY2027. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

That progression mattered because it showed that the backlog was not a single quarter's anomaly. It was built through four consecutive disclosures in which Dell raised the revenue base, lifted AI-shipment expectations or both. The company that had spent most of the 2010s digesting the EMC deal entered 2026 as one of the main fulfilment vehicles for enterprise and cloud AI infrastructure. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The CFO Transition, Correctly Dated

Dell announced on 8 September 2025 that Yvonne McGill would step down as chief financial officer effective 9 September 2025 after nearly three decades at the company, while remaining in an advisory capacity through the third quarter of fiscal 2026. David Kennedy, then a 27-year Dell veteran with prior roles including CFO of the Client Solutions Group and chief operating officer of Dell Global Sales, became chief financial officer on an interim basis on that same 9 September effective date. That was not the end state. On 25 November 2025, alongside third-quarter results, Dell named Kennedy chief financial officer on a permanent basis. By 23 May 2026, there was no open external CFO search left to describe. [Dell CFO Transition Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2025~09~dell-technologies-announces-cfo-transition.htm) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial)

## Founder Continuity, But With A Different Economic Core

As of 23 May 2026, Michael Dell had spent more than four decades running the business he founded. The continuity was real, but the enterprise he controlled in 2026 was not the same enterprise he had taken public in 1988. It was a company that had already moved through a take-private, the largest technology acquisition of its time, a complex relisting, and a major spin-off before the AI cycle arrived. By FY2026 the headline numbers were $113.5 billion of revenue and a $43 billion AI-server backlog, but the deeper historical point was that Dell had already remade itself once before the market forced it to do so again. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The 2004-2007 Interlude

Dell's timeline also put the Kevin Rollins interlude in clearer perspective than casual retellings often do. Michael Dell gave up the chief executive title in 2004, returned to it in 2007, and then never again ceded the operating top job. In hindsight that episode mattered because it reinforced how personally attached Dell remained to the company's strategic direction. The later decisions - taking the company private, levering up for EMC, collapsing the VMware tracking-stock structure and then separating VMware - were all made in a governance environment where the founder had both the formal authority and the institutional confidence to act. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline)

## Public-Market Simplification Before The AI Cycle

The VMware separation also deserves more attention than it often gets in compressed tellings of the Dell story. Before the AI cycle arrived, Dell had already spent several years simplifying a capital structure that public investors found unusually hard to model. The 2018 relisting and the 2021 VMware spin-off did not simply create cleaner charts for analysts. They also removed a structural distraction at a point when the company still needed balance-sheet flexibility and a clearer operating story. By the time AI-server demand accelerated in FY2025 and FY2026, investors were looking at a more direct hardware-and-infrastructure equity rather than at a complicated holding structure wrapped around VMware economics. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

## The Sequence Made The Reinvention Credible

That was why the FY2026 AI narrative carried more credibility than a one-quarter enthusiasm cycle. Dell had already changed the shape of the company several times. The direct-model PC business of the 1990s became the enterprise-hardware and storage business of the late 2010s; that business then became the AI-infrastructure platform of FY2026. The official chronology mattered because it showed that the latest reinvention was arriving at a company that had already proved willing to reshape itself through both organic execution and large corporate transactions. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

chapters.title: ISG, CSG, and the AI Factory
chapters.body:
## Two Franchises, One Clear Revenue Reweighting

Dell's reportable structure stayed simple even as the economics changed sharply. In FY2026, Infrastructure Solutions Group produced $60.826 billion of revenue, up 40 per cent year on year, while Client Solutions Group produced $50.984 billion, up 5 per cent. What changed was not the number of segments but their relative importance. ISG, which housed servers, storage and networking, became the company's fastest-growing and most scrutinised business because the AI-server ramp ran through it. CSG, which housed commercial and consumer PCs and related devices, remained the stabilising cash engine. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## ISG: The Infrastructure Engine

The FY2026 10-K gave a granular picture of ISG. Full-year ISG revenue consisted of $24.683 billion of AI-optimised servers and related networking, $19.512 billion of traditional servers and networking, and $16.631 billion of storage. In the fourth quarter alone, ISG reported record revenue of $19.6 billion, including record quarterly AI-optimised-server revenue of $9.0 billion, record quarterly traditional servers and networking revenue of $5.9 billion, and storage revenue of $4.8 billion. The result was not simply more server volume. It was a re-ranking of the portfolio, with AI-optimised systems becoming the segment's largest growth vector by far. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

By March 2026 Dell said more than 4,000 customers were deploying the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA. That statement did two things at once. It showed that public customer evidence extended beyond a handful of headline names, and it made clear that Dell wanted the market to read the AI business as a platform sale rather than as a spot shipment of GPU-heavy boxes. The company still did not identify the customers behind most of the more than $64 billion of FY2026 AI-server orders, but it did document that the deployment base had broadened materially. [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Storage: Still Material, No Longer The Lead Story

Storage remained a very large business inside ISG even after the AI-server ramp took over the narrative. Dell's $16.631 billion of FY2026 storage revenue reflected the legacy EMC product estate - PowerMax, PowerStore, PowerScale and Data Domain among the most important families - and it remained strategically relevant because Dell kept pitching AI infrastructure as an integrated stack spanning servers, networking and storage. What changed in FY2026 was not that storage disappeared, but that the AI-optimised-server line grew much faster than storage and became the part of ISG that investors used to handicap the stock. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## CSG: The Ballast

CSG did not stop mattering because ISG accelerated. On the contrary, it mattered because it gave Dell a large, still-profitable client business while the infrastructure side absorbed the working-capital demands of a much larger AI build-out. The 10-K said CSG generated $44.062 billion of commercial revenue and $6.922 billion of consumer revenue in FY2026. In the fourth quarter, commercial client revenue was $11.6 billion and consumer revenue was $1.9 billion. The disclosed base showed a larger and more durable client franchise than abbreviated market shorthand often implied. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Margin Reality Was More Complicated Than The Revenue Story

Profitability needed the most care. Dell's 10-K said ISG operating income rose to $7.111 billion in FY2026, but operating margin fell to 11.7 per cent from 12.8 per cent because gross margin rate decreased, primarily due to a higher mix of AI-optimised servers and related networking. CSG operating income was $2.833 billion and operating margin was 5.6 per cent, down from 6.1 per cent. In other words, Dell disclosed that the AI ramp drove much larger gross-profit dollars, but it also disclosed that the segment mix compressed the operating-margin percentage inside ISG. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

| Segment / metric | FY2026 revenue | FY2026 operating income | FY2026 operating margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ISG | $60.826B | $7.111B | 11.7% |
| CSG | $50.984B | $2.833B | 5.6% |
| Commercial client | $44.062B | included in CSG | included in CSG |
| Consumer | $6.922B | included in CSG | included in CSG |

## What Dell Actually Said About Customers

Public customer naming was narrower than the broader market narrative. Dell's FY2025 year-end release said backlog had been supported by deals booked with xAI and others. Dell and CoreWeave separately announced in December 2024 that they were extending their relationship to deliver AI at scale. And Dell said in March 2026 that more than 4,000 customers were deploying the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA. Those were real public datapoints. What Dell did not do, in its FY2026 earnings releases or 10-K, was identify which specific large customers drove most of the more than $64 billion of AI-server orders closed during FY2026. [Dell Q4 FY2025 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2) [Dell-CoreWeave Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2024~12~dell-cw-customer-announce.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

## The Segment Question Entering FY2027

By the snapshot date, Dell's segment structure had become easier to describe and harder to model. ISG now carried the revenue momentum, but the 10-K showed that the richer AI mix had diluted segment margin percentage. CSG no longer dictated the growth narrative, but it still mattered as the large installed-base franchise that kept the company diversified. The operating question for FY2027 was whether the AI backlog would keep shifting absolute profit dollars into ISG fast enough to outweigh that percentage-margin compression. Dell's own disclosures narrowed the debate to that conversion problem. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Quarterly Segment Progression

The quarterly cadence gave the segment shift more texture than the full-year numbers alone. ISG revenue moved from $10.3 billion in the first quarter to $16.8 billion in the second, $14.1 billion in the third and $19.6 billion in the fourth. CSG revenue was steadier: $12.5 billion, $12.5 billion, $12.5 billion and then $13.5 billion in the fourth quarter. The pattern mattered. ISG was volatile because it was absorbing large AI orders and shipment timing; CSG was steadier because the client cycle moved at a more traditional enterprise pace. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

| Quarter | ISG revenue | CSG revenue | Most important disclosed detail |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Q1 FY2026 | $10.3B | $12.5B | $12.1B of AI orders; $14.4B backlog |
| Q2 FY2026 | $16.8B | $12.5B | $10B of first-half AI shipments |
| Q3 FY2026 | $14.1B | $12.5B | $18.4B backlog; nearly $30B of AI orders YTD |
| Q4 FY2026 | $19.6B | $13.5B | $43B backlog entering FY2027 |

## Why The Two Segments Still Belonged Together

Dell's disclosures also made clear why it continued to insist on the combined story rather than present ISG as a stand-alone growth franchise. The commercial client business remained large enough to matter operationally and financially, while the infrastructure business had become large enough to define valuation. That coexistence was not cosmetic. It meant Dell could go after a much larger AI opportunity without turning itself into a single-line hardware company whose fortunes rose and fell with one product family alone. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

chapters.title: $113.5B revenue, $43B backlog, and the operating leverage debate
chapters.body:
## The Year The Backlog Became The Financial Lens

Dell's FY2026 financial story could be read through one disclosed progression. In the first quarter it reported $12.1 billion of AI orders and a $14.4 billion AI backlog. In the second quarter it said first-half AI-server shipments had reached $10 billion and raised full-year shipment guidance to more than $20 billion. In the third quarter it reported another $12.3 billion of AI orders, nearly $30 billion of orders year to date, and an $18.4 billion backlog while lifting shipment guidance to roughly $25 billion. In the fourth quarter it closed the year with $24.683 billion of AI-optimised-server revenue, more than $64 billion of AI-server orders for the year, more than $25 billion of shipments and a $43 billion backlog entering FY2027. The central financial question was therefore not whether demand existed, but how those orders converted into revenue and profit. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Revenue, Operating Income And The Size Of The Mix Shift

The 10-K reported $113.538 billion of FY2026 revenue and $8.149 billion of operating income. ISG contributed $60.826 billion of revenue and $7.111 billion of operating income; CSG contributed $50.984 billion of revenue and $2.833 billion of operating income. In the fourth quarter, Dell reported $33.379 billion of revenue, $3.092 billion of operating income and record quarterly ISG revenue of $19.6 billion. The revenue surge was real, but so was the mix shift. AI-optimised servers were now a huge slice of the top line, and the rest of the financial statements had to absorb that change. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Margin Debate Needed A Primary-Source Reset

Dell's own filings gave a firmer answer on AI-server margins, even if not a full one. The company did **not** separately disclose AI-server gross margin. What it did disclose was that ISG operating margin fell to 11.7 per cent from 12.8 per cent because the gross-margin rate declined, primarily due to a higher mix of AI-optimised servers and related networking. CSG operating margin also moved down, to 5.6 per cent from 6.1 per cent. That meant the correct reading of FY2026 was not that AI made the business obviously more profitable on a percentage basis. The correct reading was that AI made the business much larger, while the disclosed segment data showed some percentage-margin dilution from that richer AI mix. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2026 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Consolidated revenue | $95.6B | $113.5B |
| Consolidated operating income | $6.2B | $8.1B |
| ISG operating margin | 12.8% | 11.7% |
| CSG operating margin | 6.1% | 5.6% |

## Cash Generation, Balance Sheet And Capital Return

Dell still generated meaningful cash even while carrying the AI ramp. The 10-K reported $11.185 billion of cash from operating activities in FY2026. The year-end release said Dell returned a record $7.5 billion to shareholders during the fiscal year, including repurchases and dividends, and increased both the annual cash dividend and the share-repurchase authorisation. The balance sheet remained levered by ordinary hardware standards: the 10-K showed $31.8 billion of total debt at 30 January 2026, though Dell said after year-end that it had repaid the remaining $0.5 billion of June 2026 notes. Those facts mattered because the backlog conversion story sat on top of a company that was still funding working capital, servicing debt and returning capital simultaneously. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Order Book By Quarter

One way to see the acceleration was to read the year in increments rather than in the year-end total. The first-quarter disclosure - $12.1 billion of AI orders - already exceeded what many hardware companies would call a major annual win cycle. By the end of the third quarter, Dell had disclosed nearly $30 billion of AI orders year to date and an $18.4 billion backlog. That arithmetic implied that the fourth quarter did not merely close out the year; it transformed it. If FY2026 orders exceeded $64 billion and orders through the third quarter were nearly $30 billion, then more than $34 billion of orders were booked in the fourth quarter alone or were captured in the year-end update beyond the third-quarter year-to-date figure. Dell did not break that quarter's order book out further in the release, but the step-up was visible in the disclosed totals. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The CFO Issue Was Resolved Before The Frozen Window Closed

Dell announced the transition on 8 September 2025, made Kennedy chief financial officer on an interim basis effective 9 September, and then made him permanent CFO on 25 November 2025. By the time the company filed the FY2026 10-K and entered late May 2026, the public governance fact pattern was settled. Investors could still debate Kennedy's style or the long-term shape of finance leadership, but they could not accurately describe the company as still searching for a permanent CFO. [Dell CFO Transition Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2025~09~dell-technologies-announces-cfo-transition.htm) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## What The Disclosed Numbers Did And Did Not Prove

Dell's FY2026 financial disclosures proved four things. First, the revenue ramp was real: consolidated revenue reached $113.5 billion and AI-optimised-server revenue reached $24.683 billion. Second, demand extended beyond recognised revenue: orders exceeded $64 billion and backlog ended at $43 billion. Third, the company still generated large cash flows and returned capital. Fourth, the richer AI mix pressured ISG operating margin percentage even as the segment grew much larger. What the disclosures did **not** prove was the precise gross-margin quality of each AI-server dollar or how quickly the backlog would refill once shipped. Those remained the key modelling judgments for FY2027. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Guidance Ladder

Dell's quarterly guidance changes were part of the financial story, not an afterthought. In the first-quarter release it guided full-year revenue to $101 billion to $105 billion. In the second-quarter release it raised that range to $105 billion to $109 billion and pushed AI-server shipment expectations above $20 billion. In the third-quarter release it raised full-year revenue guidance again, to $111.2 billion to $112.2 billion, while taking AI-server shipment expectations to roughly $25 billion. By the fourth-quarter release the company was no longer guiding FY2026; it was guiding FY2027 revenue to $138 billion to $142 billion and FY2027 AI-optimised-server revenue to roughly $50 billion. The year therefore featured not just revenue growth, but a repeated upward reset of management's own frame. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Working Capital Was The Hidden Variable

The order-and-backlog disclosures also pointed to a less glamorous but critical financial issue: working capital. Dell had more than $64 billion of AI-server orders for the year and more than $25 billion of shipments, meaning a large volume of customer commitments still had to move through procurement, manufacturing, delivery and collection. The company's operating cash flow remained large, but the shape of the AI cycle meant investors had to care about inventory, receivables and supplier timing as much as they cared about the income statement. That was another reason the 10-K's discussion of supplier dependence and cash generation mattered alongside the headline revenue figures. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Capital Return Was A Choice, Not A Default

Dell's record $7.5 billion of capital returned to shareholders in FY2026 was therefore noteworthy not only because it was large, but because it came during the biggest fulfilment build-out in the company's recent history. The decision to keep repurchasing stock and paying dividends while also carrying a large debt balance and a rapidly scaling AI backlog signalled confidence in cash-generation durability. It also meant the capital-allocation question for FY2027 was more nuanced than a simple growth-versus-value split. Dell was trying to behave like a mature cash-returning franchise and a fast-scaling infrastructure supplier at the same time. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

chapters.title: From $24B FY25 AI ramp to $43B FY27 backlog
chapters.body:
## Four Quarters, One Re-Rating

The cleanest way to understand Dell's FY2026 was to read the earnings releases in sequence rather than to jump straight to the year-end headline. Each quarter added a new piece of evidence: first demand, then shipments, then backlog depth, then the full financial consequence. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Q1 FY2026: Demand Became Hard To Ignore

On 29 May 2025 Dell reported first-quarter revenue of $23.4 billion. ISG revenue was $10.3 billion, up 12 per cent, and CSG revenue was $12.5 billion, roughly flat year on year. The critical new disclosure was on AI: Dell said it had generated $12.1 billion of AI orders in the quarter and exited with $14.4 billion of AI backlog. The first quarter did not yet show the full revenue consequence of the cycle, but it showed that the order book had already moved to a different scale. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial)

## Q2 FY2026: Shipments Caught Up

On 28 August 2025 Dell reported second-quarter revenue of $29.8 billion, up 19 per cent year on year. ISG revenue jumped to $16.8 billion, up 38 per cent, while CSG revenue was $12.5 billion, up 4 per cent. Dell said it had shipped $10 billion of AI solutions in the first half of the fiscal year and raised full-year AI-server shipment guidance to more than $20 billion. This was the quarter that moved the story from order intake to throughput: the company was no longer just describing demand; it was proving it could manufacture and ship at much higher levels. [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial)

## Q3 FY2026: Orders, Backlog And Governance All Moved

On 25 November 2025 Dell reported third-quarter revenue of $27.0 billion, up 11 per cent. ISG revenue was $14.1 billion, up 34 per cent, and CSG revenue was $12.5 billion, down 1 per cent. The AI disclosures tightened again: Dell said it had generated $12.3 billion of AI orders in the quarter, nearly $30 billion year to date, and ended the quarter with $18.4 billion of AI backlog while raising full-year AI-server shipment expectations to roughly $25 billion. The same release also resolved the CFO question by naming David Kennedy chief financial officer on a permanent basis. [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial)

## Q4 FY2026: The Record Print

On **26 February 2026** Dell reported fourth-quarter revenue of $33.4 billion and full-year revenue of $113.5 billion. ISG delivered record quarterly revenue of $19.6 billion, including $9.0 billion of quarterly AI-optimised-server revenue, while CSG delivered $13.5 billion of quarterly revenue with commercial client revenue at $11.6 billion and consumer at $1.9 billion. For the full year Dell disclosed $24.683 billion of AI-optimised-server revenue, more than $64 billion of AI-server orders, more than $25 billion of shipments, and a $43 billion backlog entering FY2027. Management also guided FY2027 revenue to $138 billion to $142 billion and said AI-optimised-server revenue for the year was expected to be roughly $50 billion. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

| Quarter | Revenue | ISG | CSG | Key AI disclosure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Q1 FY2026 | $23.4B | $10.3B | $12.5B | $12.1B of AI orders; $14.4B backlog |
| Q2 FY2026 | $29.8B | $16.8B | $12.5B | $10B shipped in H1; FY guide raised above $20B |
| Q3 FY2026 | $27.0B | $14.1B | $12.5B | $12.3B of AI orders; nearly $30B YTD; $18.4B backlog |
| Q4 FY2026 | $33.4B | $19.6B | $13.5B | FY AI revenue $24.683B; orders > $64B; backlog $43B |

## What The Sequence Showed

The quarter-by-quarter pattern was more important than any single release. Q1 proved demand. Q2 proved shipping capacity. Q3 proved the order book kept building even after the first large delivery wave. Q4 proved the cumulative effect on revenue, backlog and forward guidance. That was why the stock's FY2026 re-rating centred on Dell's official quarterly cadence rather than on any one sell-side note or industry article. The company itself had progressively raised the factual ceiling. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Guidance Escalation

The earnings story also worked as a progression in management confidence. After the first quarter Dell was still proving that the AI pipeline could convert into a meaningful year. After the second quarter it was confident enough to raise shipment guidance materially. After the third quarter it was confident enough to move full-year revenue higher again and to say AI-server shipments should reach roughly $25 billion. After the fourth quarter it was no longer talking only about the year just finished; it was putting a roughly $50 billion FY2027 AI-optimised-server target into the market. The sequence mattered because it showed that the narrative moved from demand validation to formal guidance. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## CSG's Steadier Pattern

The client business also gave the year a second rhythm. CSG was roughly flat in the first quarter, grew modestly in the second, slipped slightly in the third and then finished with a stronger fourth quarter. That pattern helped explain why Dell's stock became more levered to ISG than to CSG as the year progressed: the client business was still large and useful, but the step-changes were coming from infrastructure. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

chapters.title: Michael Dell, Jeff Clarke, and the Silver Lake legacy
chapters.body:
## Founder Control Remained The Core Governance Fact

Dell's 2026 proxy still described a company built around founder control. Michael Dell remained chairman and chief executive officer, and the corporate timeline still ran from the 1984 founding through the 2013 take-private, the 2016 EMC acquisition, the 2018 relisting and the 2021 VMware spin-off with his name attached at every step. That continuity mattered because Dell's board was not supervising a hired-manager company in the ordinary sense; it was supervising a founder-controlled franchise that had already executed several balance-sheet and strategic resets under the same leader. [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm) [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline)

## Jeff Clarke Was The Key Operating Lieutenant

The most operationally important non-founder executive remained Jeff Clarke. Dell announced in December 2019 that Clarke had been appointed vice chairman and chief operating officer, with responsibility across client, infrastructure and operations. By FY2026 that meant the AI-server ramp, the traditional server and storage portfolio, and the client-device base all ran through the same operating executive. Dell's own leadership materials continued to describe Clarke as vice chairman and chief operating officer. [Dell Appoints Jeff Clarke Vice Chairman and COO](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/2019/12/20191202-01.htm) [Jeff Clarke Leadership Bio](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/about-us/leadership/jeff-clarke.htm)

## The Commercial Bench Was Long-Tenured

Bill Scannell remained president of global sales and customer operations, a role Dell's own materials framed around the full enterprise and commercial customer base rather than around any single product line. That mattered because Dell's AI opportunity was sold through the same global account architecture that had long sold PCs, storage and data-centre systems. The company also kept Chuck Whitten as co-chief operating officer, a title Dell announced in June 2021 when it elevated him after a period leading transformation work. The dual structure only made sense if Dell believed it needed one operator deeply wired into product and supply chain and another focused on broader go-to-market execution and transformation. [Bill Scannell Leadership Materials](https://www.dell.com/en-us/blog/authors/bill-scannell/) [Dell Appoints Chuck Whitten Co-Chief Operating Officer](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2021~06~20210614-dell-technologies-appoints-chuck-whitten-co-chief-operating-officer.htm)

## The CFO Story Had Moved On

Dell's official chronology on David Kennedy was straightforward. On 8 September 2025 it announced that Yvonne McGill would step down as CFO effective 9 September after nearly 30 years with the company, while remaining in an advisory role through the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Kennedy, then a 27-year Dell veteran with earlier roles including CSG CFO and chief operating officer of Dell Global Sales, became chief financial officer on an interim basis on that same effective date. On 25 November 2025, Dell named Kennedy chief financial officer on a permanent basis. By 23 May 2026, the public company governance issue was no longer an open search but a settled appointment. [Dell CFO Transition Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2025~09~dell-technologies-announces-cfo-transition.htm) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [David Kennedy Leadership Materials](https://www.dell.com/en-us/blog/authors/david-kennedy/)

## The Board Was Small And Operationally Weighted

Dell's FY2026 proxy nominated eight directors: Michael Dell, Ellen Kullman, Egon Durban, David Dorman, David Grain, William Green, Steven Mollenkopf and Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich. That line-up was notable for how heavily it leaned toward current or former operating leaders rather than toward pure capital-markets specialists. Kullman had led DuPont; Green had led Accenture; Mollenkopf had led Qualcomm; Durban brought the Silver Lake capital-markets relationship that had been central since the take-private. The board also gave formal support to the Texas redomestication proposal, again underscoring that it was operating more as a strategic and structural board than as a board built around quarterly management turnover. [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm) [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication)

## What Leadership Meant For The Investment Case

The leadership picture entering FY2027 therefore had two defining traits. First, control remained concentrated with the founder and a very stable operating bench. Second, the one visible senior transition - the CFO change - had already been resolved before 23 May 2026. That left the investment debate focused less on managerial instability and more on whether a long-tenured team could keep converting AI demand into revenue without giving away too much margin. Dell's own disclosures supported that framing more than the older unresolved-CFO narrative did. [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Board In More Detail

The proxy gave the board a more specific shape than generic governance summaries usually do. Ellen Kullman remained lead independent director and chaired no operating unit, which mattered because that role sat at the centre of independent oversight in a founder-controlled company. Egon Durban remained the director most directly associated with the Silver Lake relationship and the take-private era. William Green chaired the audit committee. Steven Mollenkopf brought direct semiconductor-industry experience from Qualcomm. David Dorman and David Grain added telecommunications and infrastructure-investing perspectives, while Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich rounded out the independent slate. Read together, the list looked less like a board assembled for frequent management turnover and more like one assembled for long-cycle strategic supervision. [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

## Why Clarke's Role Was So Central

Clarke's importance also went beyond a title. Dell's own December 2019 announcement tied him not only to operations but to a broad remit across client, infrastructure and the supply chain. That meant the same executive effectively sat at the junction where Dell's two segments met. In a year when the company had to convert large AI orders into shipped systems while still running a global client-device base, that mattered enormously. The operating model was not split between disconnected baronies; it was concentrated in a single lieutenant beneath Michael Dell. [Dell Appoints Jeff Clarke Vice Chairman and COO](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/2019/12/20191202-01.htm) [Jeff Clarke Leadership Bio](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/about-us/leadership/jeff-clarke.htm)

## The Commercial Layer Was Not Cosmetic

Bill Scannell and Chuck Whitten also mattered because Dell's AI cycle still depended on go-to-market execution, not just on factory throughput. Scannell's role in global sales and customer operations meant the client business, the traditional infrastructure business and the AI business all still ran through a shared customer organisation. Whitten's co-COO role signalled that Dell wanted dedicated top-level attention on transformation and customer execution while Clarke remained the central operating counterpart on product and supply chain. The titles would have meant less at a smaller company. At Dell's scale they were a clue to how management was dividing a very large workload. [Bill Scannell Leadership Materials](https://www.dell.com/en-us/blog/authors/bill-scannell/) [Dell Appoints Chuck Whitten Co-Chief Operating Officer](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2021~06~20210614-dell-technologies-appoints-chuck-whitten-co-chief-operating-officer.htm)

chapters.title: xAI, CoreWeave, Nvidia, and the ODM competitive threat
chapters.body:
## The Public Customer Record Was Narrower Than The Market Narrative

Public discussion around Dell's AI customers often ran ahead of the primary record. Dell's own disclosures were much narrower. In its FY2025 year-end release, it said it had booked deals with xAI and others that left AI-server backlog at roughly $9 billion. Separately, Dell and CoreWeave announced in December 2024 that they were extending their relationship to deliver AI at scale. What Dell did **not** do in FY2026 earnings materials was publish a customer-by-customer ledger for the more than $64 billion of AI-server orders it later said it had closed during the year. [Dell Q4 FY2025 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2) [Dell-CoreWeave Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2024~12~dell-cw-customer-announce.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Dell's Own Update Showed Breadth, Not Just A Few Trophy Names

By March 2026 Dell was trying to shift the market's language from a few giant orders to a broader deployment base. Its Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA release said more than 4,000 customers were deploying the platform. That did not answer the concentration question entirely - large accounts could still dominate the dollar value of the order book - but it did show that Dell was dealing with a visibly expanding deployment base even while withholding the identities of the accounts behind most of the year's order intake. [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

## Supply Chain Dependence Was Real And Explicit

Dell's 10-K and earnings releases made clear, if indirectly, that the AI ramp depended on third-party component availability. The company repeatedly highlighted AI-optimised servers sold through its Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, and the year-end release's backlog arithmetic - more than $64 billion of orders closed, more than $25 billion of shipments, $43 billion of backlog left - was itself evidence that fulfilment speed mattered. The 10-K also kept the standard hardware-company warnings about reliance on third-party suppliers, supply-chain continuity and the risk that component shortages could affect results. Supply-chain analysis therefore needed to stay close to what Dell actually disclosed rather than to attach too many unsourced sub-suppliers and customer names to the story. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## What CoreWeave And xAI Actually Added To The File

The xAI and CoreWeave references remained relevant once they were put on the right footing. xAI mattered because Dell itself cited deals booked with xAI and others in the FY2025 year-end release, which showed that at least part of the early AI backlog had already been anchored by large model builders before FY2026 began. CoreWeave mattered because Dell used an official customer release to say the relationship was being extended to deliver AI at scale, giving investors a real public example of a cloud customer running Dell infrastructure in the AI build-out. A longer list of named buyers could not be supported from Dell's primary disclosures available by 23 May 2026. [Dell Q4 FY2025 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2) [Dell-CoreWeave Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2024~12~dell-cw-customer-announce.htm)

## The Supply-Chain Question Entering FY2027

By the end of FY2026 the immediate commercial question was less "who were the buyers?" than "how quickly could Dell fulfil what had already been sold?" The official sequence showed why. Dell disclosed $12.1 billion of AI orders and $14.4 billion of backlog after Q1, said first-half AI shipments had reached $10 billion after Q2, reported $18.4 billion of backlog after Q3, and then closed FY2026 with more than $64 billion of orders for the year and a $43 billion backlog entering FY2027. That pattern implied that customer demand, component access and manufacturing throughput were tightly linked. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## What Could Be Said With Confidence

The source-backed customer and supply-chain picture was therefore tighter and stronger on evidence. Dell had named xAI in a year-end AI-backlog disclosure, published a customer expansion release with CoreWeave, said more than 4,000 customers were deploying the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, and documented a large gap between AI orders booked and AI systems shipped. It had **not** named all of the large customers behind FY2026 demand, and it had **not** broken backlog out by customer or configuration. That left investors with a clear picture of breadth, but not a customer-level map of order concentration. [Dell Q4 FY2025 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2) [Dell-CoreWeave Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2024~12~dell-cw-customer-announce.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## What Dell Said About Fulfilment

The company also gave investors a clear way to think about fulfilment pressure. Orders were disclosed at one pace and shipments at another. By the end of the first quarter Dell had $14.4 billion of AI backlog. By the second quarter it said first-half shipments had reached $10 billion. By the third quarter backlog had risen to $18.4 billion even after substantial deliveries. And by the fourth quarter backlog stood at $43 billion after more than $25 billion of annual AI shipments. Those figures suggested that the supply chain was scaling fast, but that demand was still outpacing the shipping cadence. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Why Services Still Mattered

Dell's public argument for staying in the middle of the AI build-out was not just that it could source hardware. It was that it could wrap design, integration, storage, networking, support and global services around the underlying accelerated systems. The CoreWeave release and the AI Factory with NVIDIA release both reinforced that framing. They presented Dell not as a commodity pass-through vendor but as a provider of integrated AI infrastructure. That positioning did not eliminate concentration or supplier risk, but it did explain why Dell thought customers would keep using the OEM channel rather than only buying bare systems. [Dell-CoreWeave Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2024~12~dell-cw-customer-announce.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

chapters.title: Where Dell sits in the AI infrastructure landscape
chapters.body:
## Scale Was Dell's First Competitive Argument

Dell's own disclosures supported a simpler competitive framing than more elaborate tier maps. By FY2026 the company had $113.5 billion of consolidated revenue, $60.826 billion of ISG revenue, $50.984 billion of CSG revenue, more than $64 billion of AI-server orders booked during the year and a $43 billion AI-server backlog entering FY2027. That scale mattered because it meant Dell competed not as a niche AI-server vendor but as a full-stack hardware franchise with a global account base, financing capability, support infrastructure and a client-device business that still touched most enterprise customers. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Integrated-Systems Pitch Was The Main Differentiator

Dell's public answer to competition was the Dell AI Factory, not a claim that it owned the core silicon. The company repeatedly described an integrated offer that combined AI-optimised servers, networking, storage, software enablement and services. By March 2026 it said more than 4,000 customers were deploying the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA. That was the competitive point Dell itself wanted investors to focus on: not just box volume, but the ability to package the surrounding infrastructure and support around the accelerators. [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Limits Of That Advantage Were Also Disclosed

The same filings also showed where the edge could narrow. Dell did not separately disclose AI-server gross margin, and the 10-K said ISG operating margin fell to 11.7 per cent from 12.8 per cent because gross margin rate declined with a higher mix of AI-optimised servers and related networking. That meant the company was winning revenue at scale, but the margin percentage on the growing mix was not obviously strengthening with it. Any competitor or direct-design supply model that forced pricing harder would matter quickly because Dell had already disclosed that the mix shift was diluting margin rate inside ISG. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## CSG Still Mattered To Competitive Position

The client business was not just a legacy appendage to the AI story. CSG generated $50.984 billion of FY2026 revenue, including $44.062 billion of commercial revenue. That gave Dell a wider enterprise relationship footprint than an infrastructure-only vendor could claim, and it kept the sales conversation broader than a single purchase order for accelerated servers. Dell did not need CSG to be the growth story for it to remain competitively relevant; it needed CSG to keep the account base and the cash-generation base large while ISG absorbed the biggest capital and execution demands. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## What The Primary Sources Supported, And What They Did Not

The primary-source record supported the argument that Dell had become one of the largest branded fulfilment channels for AI infrastructure. It supported the claim that Dell's competitive pitch centred on integrated systems rather than on proprietary silicon. It supported the conclusion that the margin debate remained open even after the revenue breakout. What it did not support was a precise external league table for every peer or a definitive public customer-by-customer breakdown of share. Dell's own disclosures therefore pointed toward an integrated-systems competition story rather than a neat published market-share table. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Direct Relationship Advantage

Dell's competitive position still began with its direct relationship model. The same company that had been built around direct selling in the PC era now used that architecture to sell servers, storage, networking and client devices into a global enterprise base. That did not make Dell immune to price competition or direct-design alternatives, but it did mean the company entered the AI cycle with a deeper installed relationship base than a single-product challenger. The scale of CSG, the breadth of ISG and the AI Factory with NVIDIA all sat on top of that older direct model rather than replacing it. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

## Where The Disclosed Weakness Sat

The competitive weakness visible in the public filings was not lack of demand. It was the margin profile of the mix shift. Dell was plainly winning revenue and backlog at scale. But its own 10-K showed that ISG operating margin rate fell as AI-optimised servers became a larger share of the business. That meant any competitive pressure - whether from price, customer leverage or alternative fulfilment channels - would matter first through profitability rather than through an obvious collapse in orders. The filings therefore pointed toward a company that had won the right to compete at the centre of the cycle, but had not yet proved that the margin structure would strengthen alongside the revenue base. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

chapters.title: From McGill transition to record FY26 print
chapters.body:
## The Quarters That Rewrote The Franchise

Dell's catalyst calendar into 23 May 2026 was straightforward to reconstruct from primary sources. The key events were not vague sentiment shifts. They were dated earnings releases, a dated CFO transition, a dated redomestication proposal and a dated next-earnings notice. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3) [Dell CFO Transition Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2025~09~dell-technologies-announces-cfo-transition.htm) [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication)

## 29 May 2025: Q1 Made The Order Book Visible

The first-quarter FY2026 release on 29 May 2025 was the first major catalyst because it put a large hard number on AI demand. Dell reported $23.4 billion of revenue, $12.1 billion of AI orders in the quarter and $14.4 billion of AI backlog. That was enough to move the conversation from "Dell has AI exposure" to "Dell is already booking AI infrastructure at a scale that can change the whole company". [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial)

## 8 September 2025 And 25 November 2025: The CFO Transition Started, Then Ended

The finance transition happened in two steps, not one lingering state. On 8 September 2025 Dell said Yvonne McGill would step down as CFO effective 9 September and that David Kennedy would become chief financial officer on an interim basis. On 25 November 2025, when Dell released third-quarter results, it named Kennedy chief financial officer on a permanent basis. Any description of the transition as unresolved into spring 2026 would have been inaccurate. [Dell CFO Transition Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2025~09~dell-technologies-announces-cfo-transition.htm) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial)

## 28 August 2025 And 25 November 2025: Q2 And Q3 Proved The Backlog Was Building

The second-quarter release on 28 August 2025 was a catalyst because it showed that Dell could actually ship at the rate implied by the order narrative. Revenue reached $29.8 billion, ISG reached $16.8 billion, and the company said first-half AI-server shipments had reached $10 billion while full-year shipment guidance was raised above $20 billion. The third-quarter release on 25 November 2025 then showed that the order book had not cooled. Revenue was $27.0 billion, AI orders in the quarter were $12.3 billion, AI orders year to date were nearly $30 billion, and backlog had reached $18.4 billion while shipment guidance was pushed to roughly $25 billion. Those were successive catalysts because they kept proving both demand and throughput.
