[Dell Q2 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial)

## 26 February 2026: The Record Print

The defining event was the fourth-quarter and full-year release on **26 February 2026**. Dell reported $33.4 billion of quarterly revenue, $113.5 billion of FY2026 revenue, $24.683 billion of FY2026 AI-optimised-server revenue, more than $64 billion of FY2026 AI-server orders, more than $25 billion of FY2026 AI-server shipments and a $43 billion backlog entering FY2027. The same release guided FY2027 revenue to $138 billion to $142 billion and said FY2027 AI-optimised-server revenue was expected to be roughly $50 billion. That was the event that turned the backlog into the central forward valuation variable. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## 4 May 2026: Texas Redomestication Became A Formal Vote

On 4 May 2026 Dell said its board had unanimously recommended a redomestication from Delaware to Texas. The company tied the proposal to the annual meeting scheduled for 25 June 2026. This was not a revenue catalyst in the way the earnings releases were, but it was a real corporate-governance milestone inside the period under review. [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

## The Missing 'Specialist Commentary' Gap Was Better Filled By The Actual Calendar

Dell's own forward calendar framed the next catalysts more clearly than outside commentary did. By the snapshot date, Dell's investor-relations site had already posted that the company would hold a conference call on 28 May 2026 to discuss first-quarter fiscal 2027 results. Taken together with the scheduled 25 June 2026 annual meeting and redomestication vote, the company had already laid out the next two dated checkpoints that investors were waiting for. [Dell IR Press Release Index](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/press-release) [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication)

## The Catalyst Sequence In One Table

| Date | Event | Why it mattered |
|---|---|---|
| 29 May 2025 | Q1 FY2026 results | $12.1B of AI orders; $14.4B backlog |
| 28 Aug. 2025 | Q2 FY2026 results | $10B of first-half AI shipments; shipment guide raised |
| 8 Sep. 2025 | CFO transition announced | McGill stepped down; Kennedy became interim CFO |
| 25 Nov. 2025 | Q3 FY2026 results | AI orders nearly $30B YTD; backlog $18.4B; Kennedy became permanent CFO |
| 26 Feb. 2026 | Q4 and FY2026 results | FY2026 AI revenue $24.683B; orders > $64B; backlog $43B; FY2027 AI guide roughly $50B |
| 4 May 2026 | Texas redomestication recommended | Stockholder vote set for 25 June 2026 |
| 28 May 2026 | Q1 FY2027 call scheduled | First post-year-end read on backlog conversion, as scheduled before snapshot |

## What Stayed On The Calendar

By 23 May 2026, Dell's next catalysts were therefore already public and concrete. The company had not yet reported first-quarter FY2027 results, so the scheduled date remained the last relevant fact in the record. But it had already told investors when the next revenue checkpoint would come and when the Texas vote would be held. [Dell IR Press Release Index](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/press-release) [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication)

## 16 March 2026: Dell Tried To Broaden The AI Narrative

Another useful catalyst inside the period was Dell's 16 March 2026 AI Factory with NVIDIA announcement. The release said more than 4,000 customers were deploying the platform and positioned Dell as a provider of integrated AI infrastructure rather than simply as a seller of high-ticket server nodes. For investors reading Dell through the lens of a few hyperscaler orders, that release was a deliberate attempt by the company to broaden the story. [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

## 14 May 2026: The Next Quarter Was Already On The Calendar

By mid-May Dell had also posted the timing of the next earnings checkpoint. Its investor-relations site said the company would hold a conference call on 28 May 2026 to discuss first-quarter fiscal 2027 results. That mattered because it fixed the market's next test date for the backlog-conversion story before any new quarter's numbers had entered the record. [Dell IR Press Release Index](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/press-release)

chapters.title: Dell AI Factory IP and the 40-year supply-chain engineering
chapters.body:
## The Patent Record Was Disclosed, Not Absent

The FY2026 10-K separately disclosed Dell's patent count. Dell said that, as of 30 January 2026, it held 25,859 granted patents and 8,189 pending patent applications worldwide. The same filing also said the company was not substantially dependent on any single patent or group of patents. Dell therefore had a very large portfolio, but it did not present itself as a business whose economics depended on one crown-jewel patent family. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## R&D Spend Was Also Disclosed

Dell's filings also gave hard numbers on research and development. The 10-K reported $3.142 billion of company-wide R&D expense in FY2026. Of that, ISG accounted for $2.236 billion and CSG accounted for $562 million; the balance sat outside the segment allocations. That split was useful because it showed where Dell was actually spending. The larger R&D bill remained attached to infrastructure, which was consistent with a year in which AI-optimised servers became the central growth engine. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## The Durable IP Was Integration, Not Core Silicon

Dell's filings and product releases pointed to a familiar boundary line. Dell did not own the accelerators that defined the AI-server cycle. Its AI Factory disclosures explicitly centred on NVIDIA, and the company's value-add sat in system design, thermal engineering, rack integration, storage, networking, services and global deployment rather than in the GPU die itself. That did not make the IP unimportant. It made it operational rather than fab-like. Dell's defensible know-how was in turning third-party silicon into validated, deployable enterprise systems at scale. [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## EMC Still Showed Up In The Product Stack

The 2016 EMC acquisition remained central to Dell's IP and product architecture. PowerMax, PowerStore, PowerScale and Data Domain all traced through the broader storage estate Dell assembled or inherited before and through the EMC transaction. That mattered to the AI story because Dell kept presenting AI infrastructure as an end-to-end stack: accelerated compute plus networking plus storage plus services. The company did not need storage to grow like AI servers to make it strategically relevant; it needed storage to keep the integrated-systems proposition credible. [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

## Software Was A Boundary, Not The Moat

Dell did not disclose a large proprietary AI software moat comparable to the accelerator vendors' ecosystems. The company's public AI framing kept pointing instead to validation and deployment: Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, not a Dell-owned analogue to CUDA. That distinction mattered because it explained why Dell could participate in the AI capex cycle at enormous revenue scale while still leaving the software control layer primarily to partners and open ecosystems. [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

## Employee Scale Gave Context To The R&D Base

Dell also disclosed that it employed approximately 97,000 team members as of 30 January 2026. What it did **not** do was break that workforce down into R&D headcount by location or by business line. The public record therefore supported use of the disclosed company-wide employee base and the disclosed R&D spending rather than any implied site-by-site engineering ledger. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## What The Primary Sources Actually Supported

The primary-source picture of Dell's IP and R&D posture was more grounded than the public shorthand around it. Dell had a very large patent estate. It spent more than $3.1 billion on R&D in FY2026, with the heavier allocation going to ISG. It kept pitching the AI opportunity as an integration problem rather than as a proprietary-chip problem. And it still relied on the EMC-era storage portfolio to make the infrastructure stack broad enough to matter. That set of facts described a company whose moat lay in systems engineering, product breadth and operating scale more than in a single discrete invention. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline)

## Segment Allocation Mattered More Than The Aggregate Alone

The split between ISG and CSG R&D was especially instructive. ISG's $2.236 billion of R&D expense was roughly four times CSG's $562 million. That aligned with the broader financial story of FY2026: the larger incremental engineering burden sat in infrastructure, where Dell was integrating accelerated servers, storage and networking into a much more demanding product mix. CSG remained a large business, but the R&D allocation showed which segment was carrying the heavier technical load in the year under review. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## The Patent Numbers Described Breadth, Not A Single Moat

The patent counts supported the same reading. A portfolio of 25,859 granted patents and 8,189 pending applications was too large to dismiss, but Dell's own filing language steered away from claiming dependence on any one family. That was consistent with the operating model. Dell's value lay less in one irreplaceable invention than in an accumulation of systems, thermal, storage, firmware and product-design know-how built across many hardware generations. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

chapters.title: ODM self-sourcing, AI capex cycle, and the CFO transition
chapters.body:
## The Backlog Was The Opportunity, But Also The Risk Container

Dell entered FY2027 with a $43 billion AI-server backlog after saying it had closed more than $64 billion of AI-server orders and shipped more than $25 billion during FY2026. Those same numbers created the principal risk frame. If conversion stayed strong, the backlog offered unusual visibility. If component access, customer timing or pricing moved the wrong way, the same backlog could turn into delayed revenue or lower-margin revenue. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Margin Mix Was A Disclosed Risk, Not Just An Analyst Theory

Dell's own 10-K gave the best risk marker on profitability. ISG operating margin fell to 11.7 per cent in FY2026 from 12.8 per cent in FY2025 because gross-margin rate declined, primarily due to a higher mix of AI-optimised servers and related networking. That was one of the most important risk disclosures in the file because it showed, in Dell's own language, that the revenue mix supporting the bull case was already pressuring percentage margins. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## Supplier Dependence And Fulfilment Timing

Dell's filings remained explicit that the company depended on third-party suppliers and global supply-chain execution. The AI Factory releases also made clear that the current cycle was deeply tied to NVIDIA-based infrastructure. In practice, the FY2026 order-to-shipment gap - more than $64 billion of orders versus more than $25 billion of shipments - showed that fulfilment timing was not a trivial issue. A company can only convert backlog as fast as it can secure parts, assemble systems and deliver them. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Customer Concentration Was Real Even If Names Were Sparse

Dell did not provide a customer-by-customer breakout of AI demand, which limited precision but not inference. Orders of more than $64 billion in a single fiscal year plainly implied a set of very large accounts. The public customer evidence available by 23 May 2026 consisted of Dell's FY2025 note that deals had been booked with xAI and others, the CoreWeave customer release, and Dell's later statement that more than 4,000 customers were deploying the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA. That combination suggested both concentration at the top end and growing breadth beneath it. The risk was not that Dell had no customer base; it was that a relatively small number of very large customers could still matter disproportionately to backlog conversion. [Dell Q4 FY2025 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2) [Dell-CoreWeave Release](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2024~12~dell-cw-customer-announce.htm) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Capital Intensity And Balance-Sheet Pressure

The company still had to carry the balance-sheet consequences of scaling this business. Dell reported $11.185 billion of FY2026 operating cash flow, but it also reported $31.8 billion of total debt at year-end and returned a record $7.5 billion to shareholders during the year. None of those facts by itself created a crisis. Together they showed that Dell was balancing backlog fulfilment, debt management and shareholder returns at the same time. A hardware ramp of this size did not happen in a financial vacuum. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Governance Risk Was Lower Than The Operating Risks

The CFO transition no longer belonged on the active-risk list in the same way that supplier or customer concentration did. Dell had already made Kennedy permanent CFO in November 2025. The Texas redomestication, meanwhile, was a real governance item but not an operating shock; the board recommended it unanimously and tied it to the 25 June 2026 annual meeting. Those items still belonged in the diligence file, but they did not sit in the same risk tier as supplier dependence, customer concentration or mix-driven margin pressure. [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

## The Risk Picture On The Primary Record

On the primary-source record, the risk case became clearer. The genuine risks were backlog conversion timing, supplier dependence, customer concentration, and the disclosed fact that a richer AI mix had compressed ISG operating margin percentage. Those were enough. They did not need speculative numbers or unsupported customer rosters layered on top. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Execution Risk Inside The Backlog

Backlog itself carried execution risk even before any macro shock was introduced. A $43 billion queue meant a very large volume of systems still had to be configured, sourced, assembled, shipped and accepted. Dell's quarter-by-quarter disclosures showed that shipments were rising rapidly, but they also showed that order intake could outrun fulfilment for long stretches. The operational risk was therefore not abstract. It was embedded in the disclosed gap between bookings and deliveries. [Dell Q1 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## Capital Allocation Was A Secondary Risk Layer

Dell's choice to return record capital to shareholders while also carrying a large debt load and a rapidly scaling AI backlog created a second layer of risk. The company was not simply deciding how to maximise next-quarter earnings. It was deciding how much financial flexibility to preserve while fulfilling one of the largest order books in its history. If the cycle stayed strong, that balance could look disciplined. If component timing or customer schedules moved unfavourably, the same balance could begin to look tight. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

chapters.title: FY27 backlog conversion and the AI PC refresh cycle
chapters.body:
## Dell Had Already Given Formal FY2027 Guidance

Dell had **already** provided formal FY2027 guidance in its 26 February 2026 year-end release. It said full-year revenue was expected to be between $138 billion and $142 billion, and it said AI-optimised-server revenue for FY2027 was expected to be roughly $50 billion. For the first quarter, it guided revenue to $34.7 billion plus or minus $500 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $1.65 plus or minus $0.10. Any suggestion that a $40 billion-$50 billion AI-revenue frame was merely external extrapolation rather than management guidance was therefore incorrect. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The Starting Position Was Unusually Visible

Dell entered that guidance year with a $43 billion AI-server backlog and a FY2026 baseline of $24.683 billion of AI-optimised-server revenue. That gave the market a more tangible starting point than it usually had for a hardware year. The company's own guidance did not guarantee conversion speed or margins, but it did show that management believed the order book was large enough to support another substantial step up in recognised AI revenue. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## The Margin Question Carried Into FY2027

The financial challenge for the new year was also spelled out clearly by the 10-K. ISG operating margin had fallen to 11.7 per cent in FY2026 from 12.8 per cent because the gross-margin rate declined, primarily due to the richer mix of AI-optimised servers and related networking. That meant FY2027 was not only a volume story. It was a quality-of-revenue story. If the roughly $50 billion AI-revenue target was achieved with similar mix pressure, revenue could surge without a matching increase in percentage margins. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## CSG Still Provided The Cushion

Dell's outlook was not built on ISG alone. CSG had produced $50.984 billion of FY2026 revenue, including $44.062 billion of commercial revenue. Even if the growth narrative had shifted decisively toward infrastructure, the client business still mattered because it diversified the earnings base and supported cash generation while the AI-server cycle consumed more working capital. The right way to read FY2027 was therefore as a two-part story: very large AI-infrastructure growth on one side and a still-material commercial client franchise on the other. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## The Near-Term Calendar Was Public Before The Snapshot Date

By 23 May 2026, investors also knew when the next datapoints were due. Dell's investor-relations site had already posted that the company would hold a conference call on 28 May 2026 to discuss first-quarter fiscal 2027 results. Separately, the board's Texas redomestication proposal was set for a vote at the 25 June 2026 annual meeting. Those events sat ahead of the snapshot date as scheduled catalysts, even though their outcomes had not yet entered the public record. [Dell IR Press Release Index](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/press-release) [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

## The CFO Question No Longer Belonged In The Forward Debate

Dell's finance leadership was already settled before FY2027 began in earnest. Kennedy had moved from interim CFO to permanent CFO on 25 November 2025. The forward debate therefore belonged on backlog conversion, shipment pacing, revenue mix and demand durability rather than on whether Dell still needed to find a finance chief. [Dell Q3 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## The Real Outlook Question

On the primary-source record, the outlook came down to one question. Could Dell translate a $43 billion AI-server backlog and a roughly $50 billion FY2027 AI-revenue target into revenue growth that remained economically attractive after supplier constraints, customer concentration and mix-driven margin pressure were taken into account? The official guidance answered the direction of travel. The next earnings releases were going to answer the pace and the quality of that travel. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## What The FY2027 Guide Implied

Dell's own guidance implied a very large step-up even before any additional upside case was layered on. FY2026 AI-optimised-server revenue was $24.683 billion. The FY2027 guide called for roughly $50 billion. That implied roughly a doubling of the AI revenue line in a single year, even though the company had already reported one of the largest hardware ramps in the sector during FY2026. The fact that management was willing to publish that figure made the year-end release more consequential than a normal hardware-company guide. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3)

## The First Quarter Was Set Up As A Conversion Test

The scheduled 28 May 2026 first-quarter call mattered because it was the first chance for Dell to show whether the year-end backlog was turning into recognised revenue at the pace implied by the new guide. Investors did not need a full fiscal year to start judging the story; they needed an early read on shipment cadence, backlog movement and the tone of management's commentary. That was why the May earnings date and the June redomestication vote were the two public markers immediately ahead of the snapshot date. [Dell IR Press Release Index](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/press-release) [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

## CSG's Role In The Outlook

CSG also remained part of the forward picture, even if it was no longer the market's first question. A business that had generated $50.984 billion of revenue in FY2026 still shaped the base from which Dell would fund working capital and defend customer relationships. The outlook was therefore not simply "AI up or down". It was "AI ramps on top of a still-large client franchise". That was one reason Dell could present such a large AI target without presenting itself as a single-product company. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

## Glossary

**AI Factory.** Dell's branded architecture for integrated AI infrastructure. In March 2026 Dell said more than 4,000 customers were deploying the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA. [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

**AI-optimised servers.** Dell's disclosed high-growth AI-server category inside ISG. The company reported $24.683 billion of FY2026 AI-optimised-server revenue, more than $64 billion of FY2026 AI-server orders and a $43 billion backlog entering FY2027. [Dell Q4 FY2026 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-3) [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

**CSG (Client Solutions Group).** Dell's client-device segment. It generated $50.984 billion of FY2026 revenue, including $44.062 billion of commercial revenue and $6.922 billion of consumer revenue. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

**H100 / H200.** NVIDIA Hopper-generation accelerators that anchored the first large wave of Dell AI-server deployments. Dell's own FY2025 and FY2026 disclosures did not break backlog out by GPU model, but the AI Factory with NVIDIA framing made the NVIDIA partnership central to the cycle. [Dell Q4 FY2025 Results](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2) [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

**ISG (Infrastructure Solutions Group).** Dell's infrastructure segment, covering servers, storage and networking. It produced $60.826 billion of FY2026 revenue and $7.111 billion of operating income. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

**NPU (Neural Processing Unit).** A dedicated processor block used for on-device AI inference in modern PCs. Dell used the broader AI-PC theme in its client narrative, but the FY2026 filings disclosed the client results primarily through commercial and consumer revenue rather than through a separate NPU metric. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

**ODM (Original Design Manufacturer).** A contract manufacturer or design partner that large customers can use as an alternative to branded OEM procurement. Dell's filings did not provide a public league table of ODM share, but the risk that large customers have alternatives remained part of the competitive backdrop. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm)

**PowerEdge.** Dell's core server family. The AI-optimised-server ramp ran through PowerEdge-based infrastructure sold under the Dell AI Factory umbrella. [Dell AI Factory With NVIDIA Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-ai-factory-nvidia-delivers-proven-path-enterprise-ai-roi)

**PowerScale / PowerStore / PowerMax.** Major Dell storage families that remained relevant to the integrated infrastructure pitch after the EMC acquisition. [Dell FY2026 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199626000008/dell-20260130.htm) [Dell Corporate Timeline](https://www.dell.com/en-us/lp/dt/timeline)

**Texas redomestication.** The board-approved proposal to change Dell's state of incorporation from Delaware to Texas, scheduled for a stockholder vote at the 25 June 2026 annual meeting. [Dell Redomestication Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-board-unanimously-recommends-redomestication) [Dell FY2026 Proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000119312526226734/d132444ddef14a.htm)

| ISG revenue | $60.826B | $19.6B | Q4 included $9.0B of AI-optimised-server revenue |

| ISG operating income | $7.111B | n/a | Operating margin 11.7% |
| CSG operating income | $2.833B | n/a | Operating margin 5.6% |

founder_chairman_ceo.name: Michael S. Dell
founder_chairman_ceo.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
founder_chairman_ceo.tenure_summary: Founder; CEO 1984-2004 and from 2007-present; Chairman continuously since 1984
founder_chairman_ceo.framing: Dell founded the original Dell Computer Corporation in his University of Texas at Austin dorm room in 1984 at age 19. The company went public in 1988, became the dominant US PC manufacturer in the 1990s, took itself private in a $24.4B leveraged buyout in 2013 (with Silver Lake), acquired EMC in 2016 in a $67B transaction (then the largest tech deal in history), and relisted publicly in December 2018 via a complex VMware-tracking-stock exchange. Dell's ownership and operational control through these structural transformations is the single longest founder-CEO continuous franchise in US large-cap technology. He continues to chair the board and run the company day-to-day at the snapshot date.

His role coordinating with VMware CEO (during the period Dell held VMware tracking stock) made him the integration architect for the multi-platform technology stack. leadership.redomestication_to_texas: The board has unanimously recommended Dell Technologies' redomestication to Texas, consistent with the broader trend of large US companies moving from Delaware to Texas through 2025-2026. The transaction reflects Dell's Texas operating headquarters (Round Rock, TX) being the appropriate domicile rather than Delaware corporate formation.
leadership.board_composition_observation: Dell's eight-director board (Group I nominees) pairs the founder-CEO-Chairman (Michael Dell) with the Silver Lake institutional shareholder representative (Durban) and six independents. The independents are unusually weighted toward operational-CEO experience (Kullman ex-DuPont, Green ex-Accenture, Mollenkopf ex-Qualcomm, Dorman ex-AT&T) rather than financial-engineering or pure capital-markets credentials. This composition reflects Dell's operating posture as the integrated technology hardware franchise rather than as a transactional or capital-structure-driven company. The redomestication to Texas is the contemporary governance event that further aligns the corporate form with the operating reality.

counterparties.key_finding: Dell's FY2026 customer base is the broadest in US enterprise IT, but the AI server cycle has concentrated incremental revenue toward a smaller set of hyperscaler buyers (xAI, CoreWeave, Microsoft, AWS, Meta, Google, Oracle, Tesla, plus enterprise AI buyers). Supply-chain alignment with Nvidia (the dominant accelerator GPU supplier for AI server platforms) and AMD (alternative accelerator GPU and EPYC CPU supplier) is the dominant strategic relationship. Dell's AI Factory initiative — high-performance computing and liquid-cooled servers optimised for Nvidia and AMD silicon — is the product framework for hyperscaler design-in.
